frames.title: Step 2: Load data and decide when to open the scene
frames.logic: I download the public viewer data, then check the route definitions without opening VPython. I use local Jupyter for the native viewer; Colab does not provide the same interactive VPython environment. I leave the window disabled initially so Run All does not enter an endless display loop.
frames.code:
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.request import urlretrieve

work = Path("lesson-data")
work.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

def get_file(relative_path):
    # I download a public example only when its local copy is missing.
    destination = work / Path(relative_path).name
    if not destination.exists():
        urlretrieve("https://saswataiith.github.io/" + relative_path, destination)
    return destination

viewer_path = get_file("assets/examples/bicontinuity-3d/viewer.json")

viewer_data = __import__("json").loads(viewer_path.read_text())
assert viewer_data["n"] == 256
for phase in ("red", "blue"):
    for axis in "xyz":
        route = np.asarray(viewer_data["routes"][phase][axis])
        steps = (np.diff(route, axis=0) + 128) % 256 - 128
        assert np.all(np.abs(steps).sum(axis=1) == 1)
        assert np.array_equal(steps.sum(axis=0), np.eye(3, dtype=int)["xyz".index(axis)] * 256)
print("All six saved routes have face-sharing steps and the stated winding.")
frames.output: All six saved routes have face-sharing steps and the stated winding.

frames.title: Step 11: Interpolate a periodic voxel step
frames.logic: I interpolate only between consecutive verified face-sharing voxels. The shortest periodic displacement identifies a seam step. Display coordinates are wrapped back into the box.
frames.code:
if open_viewer:
    def position_at(q):
        i = min(int(q), len(route) - 2)
        t = 1 if q >= len(route) - 1 else q - i
        a, b = route[i:i + 2]
        d = [(b[j] - a[j] + n // 2) % n - n // 2 for j in range(3)]
        return [(a[j] + 0.5 + d[j] * t) % n for j in range(3)]

frames.title: Step 12: A new displayed trail
frames.logic: I create a new curve at the supplied position. A separate curve after a seam crossing avoids drawing a shortcut through the box.

frames.title: Step 13: The recorded path
frames.logic: I append only the route segments the turtle has executed. At a periodic crossing I end one trail on the face and start another at the opposite face.
frames.code:
if open_viewer:
    def extend_trail(to):
        global executed, crossings
        q = executed
        while q < to - 1e-09:
            i = min(int(q + 1e-09), len(route) - 2)
            end = min(to, i + 1)
            a, b = route[i:i + 2]
            axis = next((j for j in range(3) if abs(b[j] - a[j]) > n / 2), None)
            if axis is not None and q < i + 0.5 - 1e-09 and (end >= i + 0.5):
                face = [x + 0.5 for x in a]
                face[axis] = n if b[axis] < a[axis] else 0
                current_trail.append(pos=vec(*face))
                partner = list(face)
                partner[axis] = 0 if face[axis] == n else n
                begin_trail(partner)
                q = i + 0.5
                crossings += 1
            else:
                current_trail.append(pos=vec(*position_at(end)))
                q = end
        executed = to

frames.title: Step 14: Reset the selected route
frames.logic: I reset progress and the executed trail when the phase or winding direction changes. The saved route remains the source of the voxel positions.
frames.code:
if open_viewer:
    def reset(_=None):
        global progress, running, phase, direction, executed, crossings, route
        phase = phase_menu.selected
        direction = direction_menu.selected
        progress = 0.0
        running = False
        executed = 0.0
        crossings = 0
        route = data['routes'][phase][direction]
        for trail in trails:
            trail.clear()
            trail.visible = False
        trails.clear()
        begin_trail(position_at(0))
        visibility()
